subject.title: fix(exec-approvals): handle same-process sync/async lock contention

question: What committed-state contract should synchronous approval reads use while the same process holds an asynchronous write lock?
rationale: Choosing between eliminating the nested synchronous read and introducing an explicit process-local committed snapshot changes an authorization invariant; automation cannot safely choose which state is authoritative during an active or rollback-bound write.

options.title: Remove the nested synchronous read
options.body: Refactor the async owner path to carry its prepared policy state forward so no synchronous reader bypasses the active write lock.

options.title: Add a committed snapshot
options.body: Maintain a process-local snapshot updated only after persistence commits and serve that snapshot during same-process contention.

options.title: Accept lockless reads
options.body: Intentionally permit reads during active copy fallback writes and document that transient or rollback-bound policy state may be observed.

recommendation.title: Remove the nested synchronous read
recommendation.body: Refactor the async owner path to carry its prepared policy state forward so no synchronous reader bypasses the active write lock.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history most strongly connects this person to the approval persistence and authorization invariants involved in the decision.
